title: Toolcall bridge: semantic aliasing and fallthrough policy for OpenAI-style tools vs legacy functions
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Problem: Customers call OpenAI-style 'tools' from client SDKs. Redwood has an older 'functions' surface in some deployed runtimes and a canonical function registry in others. We need a deterministic, observable bridge so OpenAI tool calls route to the correct Redwood function without breaking streaming, structured outputs, or backward compatibility. This ticket defines the semantic aliasing and fallthrough policy: algorithmic rules to match tool names to functions, signature translation rules, how to log/meter fallthroughs, and a phased rollout plan for runtime-1.26.

Goals:
- Maximize successful automatic mappings with conservative fallbacks to avoid breaking production behavior.
- Preserve streaming behavior and token-level partial outputs when a mapped function streams results.
- Emit clear telemetry for mapping decisions to drive regression monitors and customer notifications.
- Offer an opt-in header and admin console flag during rollout to control aggressive mapping behavior.

Matching strategy (canonical order):
1) Exact canonical name match (case-sensitive).
2) Exact case-insensitive match.
3) Punctuation/whitespace normalization: strip punctuation, collapse whitespace.
4) Semantic aliasing lookup: use a precomputed alias table maintained by the platform (aliases populated from onboarding, PRD, and embeddings-based candidate generation). Matching here returns a single best candidate or none.
5) Signature-aware disambiguation: when multiple candidate functions exist, prefer the candidate whose JSON schema for args is compatible (superset/subset rules) with the incoming tool's parameters.
6) Fallback runner (last resort): route to a 'toolcall-fallback-runner' which attempts best-effort mapping at runtime, records the attempt, and returns a structured error if no safe mapping can be made.

Signature translation rules:
- OpenAI tool parameter schemas (JSON Schema-like) to Redwood function param types: apply deterministic conversion rules (number->float/int heuristics, string enums -> enum typed params, nested objects preserved with path mapping).
- If the tool requires positional args but the Redwood function expects named params, convert by parameter order only when names are semantically equivalent via alias map.
- Keep special typed parameters (file, binary, stream) unchanged and reject mapping if the runtime does not support the type.

Streaming and structured output considerations:
- If the target Redwood function returns a streaming response, forward tokens downstream and preserve functioncall markers in the stream to allow client-side incremental processing.
- For non-streaming functions called by a client expecting streaming tool output, buffer and stream with a single 'final' chunk to avoid breaking clients. Log mismatch metric.
- Structured outputs: convert Redwood structured return types to the OpenAI function call response shape. If conversion fails, return a structured error and increment conversion-failure metric.

Observability and telemetry:
- Emit a mapping_decision event with fields: incoming_tool_name, matched_function_key (or null), strategy_step (1..6), signature_match (true|false), fallback_used (true|false).
- Track metrics: mapping_success_rate, fallback_rate, signature_mismatch_rate, streaming_mismatch_rate, conversion_failure_rate.
- Expose a per-customer mapping audit log in Console for enterprise tenants (togglable by RBAC).

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (opt-in): behind header X-Redwood-OpenAITool-Compat: opt-in. Monitor metrics for 2 weeks on canary fleet.
- Phase 2 (conservative-on): enable for 10% traffic for customers with consent via account settings. Raise alerts if fallback_rate > 1% or conversion_failure_rate > 0.5%.
- Phase 3 (default-on): enable for all hosted API traffic after two approval cycles and security sign-off. Provide migration guide and bulk aliasing tool in Console.

Developer UX and admin controls:
- Console: alias table editor for tenant admins; bulk upload CSV for aliasing; audit history.
- API/SDK: new endpoint POST /compat/tool-aliases and GET /compat/tool-aliases for configuring tenant aliases. (API only for enterprise scopes).
- Header-based opt-out: X-Redwood-Toolcall-Compat: off to force strict function matching.

Security and safety trade-offs:
- Aggressive semantic aliasing may cause unintended function invocation with side-effects. Therefore default behavior is conservative matching only up to step 3; semantic aliasing and fallback runner are opt-in or rate-limited per tenant.
- All mapped calls inherit tenant RBAC and KMS contexts; ensure we never relax authorization during mapping.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit tests for each of the six strategy steps, including ambiguous name cases.
- End-to-end tests verifying streaming passthrough and buffered fallback behavior.
- Telemetry events emitted for each mapping decision and visible in canary dashboards.
- Console aliasing controls functional in QA and only visible to enterprise orgs.
- Documentation: migration guide, SDK header docs, and sample mapping CSV.

Open questions / future work:
- Should we use a learned classifier to rank alias candidates (long term) vs rule-based scoring? (favor rule-based for initial rollout).
- How aggressively to auto-suggest aliases in Console based on observed traffic? Limit to suggestions only.

notes: 2026-03-10: Ticket created after spike showing 12% of incoming OpenAI tool names do not exact-match functions; initial draft of strategy included.
2026-03-11: Spike results attached to PR #1248. Found common patterns: punctuation differences, suffixes like '_v2', and camelCase vs snake_case. Decided to include normalization step.
2026-03-12: Engineering review with Runtime and Security. Security requires conservative defaults and tenant-level opt-in for semantic aliasing. Added header flags and Console controls.
2026-03-13: UX sync: Console alias editor mockups reviewed; asked to include CSV bulk upload and audit trail. Miguel to follow up with DES for minor UI polish.
2026-03-14: Implemented basic matching steps 1-3 in runtime prototype. Next: implement alias table lookup and signature-aware disambiguation.
